mechanism_narrative: A low and declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which positively impacts consumer confidence and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following low UNRATE, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) crosses above 4.5%, it indicates monetary tightening, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows after FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both CPIAUCSL (inflation) and FEDFUNDS (interest rates) increase simultaneously, the cost of capital rises, negatively impacting corporate profitability and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows when both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) during an economic expansion signals strong demand in the housing market, which positively impacts related industries and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following an increase in HOUST, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals increased economic activity, which positively impacts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following an increase in INDPRO, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, which increases consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 5-day windows following a PAYEMS increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) growth slows while unemployment (UNRATE) rises, it indicates a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows when GDPC1 growth slows and UNRATE rises, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in real federal spending (RSAFS) during a late-cycle expansion signals reduced government stimulus, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following a slowdown in RSAFS, the hypothesis is rejected.
